full_judgment: 12. There are other grounds on which the plea of res judicata is not attracted in rectification case. It would be profitable to note that the rectification proceedings affect the interest of the public and not merely the parties before the Court. It is to be borne in mind that under the Act any person aggrieved may apply for rectification of the Register either to the High Court Division or to the Registrar. Furthermore, under section 46(4), the High Court Division or the Registrar can of its or his own motion rectify the Register. So, a duty is cast upon the High Court Division and the Registrar to make any order as referred to sub-sections (1) and (2) of section 46 to maintain the purity of the Register. No doubt a discretion is vested in the tribunal but that discretion has to be exercised judicially keeping in view the principle of justice and public interest. The discretion of the Court or the Registrar under section 46 of the Act entitles the Court or the Registrar, either to order rectification or not to do so and the question is not so much between the applicant for the rectification on the one hand and the respondent on the other but between the public and the respondent. See Kerly, 9th Edition The Law of Trade Marks and Trade Names, paragraph 383 and the decision noted thereof Noblit Sparks Industries Application (1950) 68 RPC 168.
